correctness.rationale: PASS: Full proof checks fixed-point constraints of the stable sorting permutation at content (m,m,1), eliminating starts in 0, final 2 and 1 between last non-1 letters. Removing the unique 2 leaves a binary word with at most one equal pair, forcing exactly A_m=(10)^(m-1)120 or B_m=(10)^(m-2)10201. Direct agreement counts yield A_m distance m+1 only for even m, B_m never sharp. Under conjugation by i↦i+1, the A_m sorting permutation is multiplication by a=(m+1)=2^(-1) mod p with a single splice through zero; one cycle iff p=2m+1 is prime and 2 primitive. The prime-root condition does not assume infinitely many such primes. Independent complete enumeration m=2..8 reproduces exactly two fixed-point-free candidates and sharp counts (m=2,6 only); finite checks are not the all-m proof.
